business_request.question: For the outer-race teaching scenario, describe the linked NSK example (bearing type, part and attributed operating circumstance), the general contact-wear mechanism and one lubrication-related alternative. What actual cause, if any, is established by the supplied class?

draft.answer: In the supplied NSK example, the linked case is the outer ring of the same deep-groove ball bearing as 'False Brinelling 1'; the manufacturer attributes raceway false brinelling to vibration from an external source while the bearing is stationary [EV-K01-001]. More generally, NSK describes false brinelling as contact wear — hollow spots resembling brinell dents — caused by vibration and swaying at the contact points between rolling elements and raceway, with oscillation/vibration of a stationary bearing (e.g., during transport) and small-amplitude oscillating motion listed as possible causes [EV-K01-002]. One lubrication-related alternative in the same possible-causes list is poor lubrication [EV-K01-003]. The caller-assigned class 'outer_race' does not by itself establish any actual cause: the external-vibration-during-standstill circumstance is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference, and the listed causes are possibilities rather than an observed root cause [EV-K01-001][EV-K01-002][EV-K01-003].
